subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

He came here **with a view to** **meet** his old friend.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**with a view to**" is followed by a gerund (verb + -ing), not an infinitive.
 
• In the sentence, "**with a view to meet**" is incorrect because "meet" is in its base form instead of the gerund form "meeting."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**with a view to meeting**," which is grammatically appropriate.
 
• Thus, the sentence requires modification to ensure correctness and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He came here with a view to meeting his old friend."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "to meet with"** – This phrase is not appropriate in this context as it alters the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "for meeting"** – This phrase is grammatically incorrect and does not fit the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 3: "in view to meet"** – This phrase is incorrect and ungrammatical.
